_comment: Where each unit of the paper goes: MAIN article, SUPPLEMENTARY material, or
REPOSITORY. Declared here as data, checked by tools/check_split_map.py, and NOT
yet applied -- nothing has been cut. This file is a map, and the map is made
before the cutting so that no numerical result, statistical claim or piece of
reproducibility evidence is removed by accident.
The governing rule, from the corresponding author, 30 September 2026:
scientific evidence is not hidden in the supplementary material.
So every unit that leaves MAIN must say, in main_retains, what stays in the main
article so that the conclusion it supports is still stated and still supported
there. check_split_map.py fails if any does not.
Word counts are NOT declared here. The checker reads them from the assembled
manuscript, so the projection cannot drift from the paper it projects.
_phase_note: Where applying this map has got to. 'planned' means nothing has been done;
'moved' means every unit bound for the supplement is now in
manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY.md and the two wide tables are reduced in the article
and complete there, but the sections that stay have NOT yet been condensed to
their targets; 'condensed' means they have, and at that point applied becomes
true and the checker starts requiring each section to be at or below target.
Moved on 30 September 2026: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5 and the article renumbered to
Tables 1-6. No value was deleted at any point -- see the word accounting in
tools/move_to_supplementary.py and the cell-by-cell check in
_applied_note: false means the map is a plan and the manuscript is untouched: the checker then
requires each MAIN target to be at or below the section's current length, since a
target above it is not a reduction. Set it to true only when the cutting is done;
the checker then reverses the test and requires each section to be at or below its
declared target, so the map becomes the thing that holds the article's length
rather than a record of an intention.

target.guidance_quote: Full papers, describing original work...should normally be about 5,000 words.
note: Recalculated empirically on 1 October 2026, after three condensation batches
measured what a careful condensation actually costs. The two earlier target sets
were estimates: a uniform 60 % cut of prose, then a uniform 45 %. Neither held.
What the three batches measured, each keeping every number, p-value, caveat and
coverage statement:
Batch 1  Overview, 7.1-7.2      2,489 -> 1,648   prose cut 43 %
The first classifier tried was numeric density -- numbers per 100 words of prose --
and it ordered the three batches correctly (3.5, 4.3, 4.6 against 43 %, 28 %, 20 %).
It is still the wrong classifier, because it counts how many numbers a section
MENTIONS rather than how many it OWNS. A Discussion section citing twenty results
scores as dense as a Results section establishing them, and compresses quite
differently: a borrowed number can become a pointer, an owned one cannot.
Targets are therefore computed from OWNED density: numeric values appearing in
this section and in no other, per 100 words of its prose. The bands are anchored
on the three batches and never promise a deeper cut than one of them achieved:
owned/100 >= 4.0  ->  cut 20 %   (it establishes its own evidence)
below 2.0         ->  cut 43 %   (expository, or citing what other sections own)
The measure separates the paper sharply. Section 7.3 owns 8.4 values per 100 words
and resisted condensation; 8.1, 8.2, 3.2, 6.7 and Contributions own none at all --
every number they carry is established elsewhere -- and condense like prose.
This projects the body of Sections 1-9 to about 17,500 words, from 24,881 now and
28,462 before any of this began. That is 3.5x the guide's 'about 5,000 words',
and it is a measurement rather than an aspiration: the two earlier figures, 11,371
and 13,223, were produced by assuming a cut rate instead of observing one.
The rule also finds about 2,070 words of room still inside the already-condensed
Results, concentrated in 7.6, 7.7, 7.9, 7.10 and the Overview -- sections that cite
many values and own few. Their targets are left at their achieved figures rather
than lowered, because revisiting finished work is the author’s call and not this
file’s.
tier_2_if_required: If an editor asks for a further reduction, the next three units to move whole,
in this order, are 7.3.1 (pooled against subject-averaged recall), 7.5.1
(expected calibration error) and 7.4 (between-subject against seed variation).
Each is a self-contained measurement whose headline sentence can stand in the
section above it, and together they are about 1,400 words of main text. They are
listed rather than moved because each one currently carries a claim the
Discussion leans on, and moving them needs the same main_retains discipline as
the entries below, written deliberately and not under deadline.

destinations.MAIN: Stays in the submitted article. target_words is what it should be cut to; where it equals the current count, nothing is cut.
destinations.BOTH: A reduced form in the article and the complete form in the supplementary material. Used only for tables whose full width does not fit a two-column page but whose content a reader must be able to see. main_form says what the reduced form shows.
destinations.SUPPLEMENTARY: Moves out of the article into the supplementary PDF, which is submitted with it and is part of the published record.
destinations.REPOSITORY: Belongs to the released code and data, not to either document. Used only for material that is about the verification machinery rather than about the study.

holm_ceiling_derivation.host: 6.5.1 Multiplicity, and why the analyses are reported as exploratory
holm_ceiling_derivation.reason: The derivation of each family's Holm ceiling in exact rational arithmetic, including that the five-point Spearman floor of 2/5! equals alpha/3 exactly and so the ceiling is an equality rather than a strict inequality.
holm_ceiling_derivation.main_retains: The ceilings themselves as stated values, and the sentence that no test in a Wilcoxon family of 26 or more can reject at n = 10 whatever the data. The derivation is also in the released tools/check_multiplicity.py, which re-derives it on every run.

recalibration_worked_example.reason: The fold-by-fold worked example of fitting the logistic recalibration on the other nine subjects.
recalibration_worked_example.main_retains: The protocol stated once: a per-fold logistic recalibration fitted on the nine training subjects and applied to the held-out subject, never fitted on the held-out subject. That sentence is the whole guarantee; the example only illustrates it.

per_fold_results.reason: All 750 per-fold rows. No journal prints them and no supplementary PDF should; they are a CSV.
per_fold_results.main_retains: The statement that all 750 per-fold results are released, with the address, and that every table and significance test in the paper regenerates from them without a GPU and without the recordings.
